description: Canonical registry of lifecycle decisions for state artifacts that were retired, revived, or deprecated during CPP-MS3. Each entry documents WHY the decision was made and WHAT replaces (or resurrects) it, so future sessions do not re-open closed questions.

decisions.rationale: Single-file HANDOFF.md was written per-session by per-agent-handoff.mjs as LEGACY_HANDOFF alias, but N terminals writing the same file caused lossy clobber — last writer's RESUME silently overwrote the previous one.
decisions.migration_window: immediate — legacy path still written as latest-pointer for 1-session backward-compat, then removable

decisions.rationale: Single legacy dotfile was the only destination for pre-compact survival snapshot; concurrent /precompact from 2+ terminals overwrote each other's RESUME directives.
decisions.reader: compact-restore.mjs globs SURVIVAL_DIR, picks freshest mtime within 30m, falls back to legacy file
decisions.migration_window: 1 session — legacy single file kept writable for readers that have not yet been upgraded to per-instance glob pattern

decisions.rationale: File existed as 3-byte `{}` zombie despite 6+ hook references that assumed populated content. Readers received empty objects and silently no-oped; the feature-cascade propagation chain was effectively dead.
decisions.replacement: same path — populated with canonical v1.0.0 schema {schemaVersion, event, timestamp, system_counts{}, recent_additions{}, feature_cascade{}}
decisions.replacement_engine: SessionEventLogEngine (writer) + compact-restore.mjs (reader, emits Feature Cascade block)
current_writers_post_retirement: CPP-MS3 Session 7 populated schema + seed data
Future sessions: append to recent_additions when new engines/hooks/skills ship

decisions.rationale: Same 3-byte zombie pattern as SESSION_ARTIFACTS.json — file existed but was empty, so post-compact hooks that appended lifecycle events silently dropped them.
decisions.replacement: same path — populated with canonical v1.0.0 schema {schemaVersion, events[]}
